metadata.rationale: box + b is the button glyph; single ink color becomes fill.
the letter picks the op, the word in the same box becomes its label.
glyph reading is case-insensitive: B == b == button.
glyph box whose center sits within 48px of the artboard center snaps center_in_region.
confidence below 0.35 always waits, even on a clean glyph read.
box + i is the image glyph; no ink color and no text means no params at all.
uppercase I maps to image under the case-insensitive rule.
square snapping is a plain-shape policy; glyph components snap only for navbar or centering.
a word in an i-box routes to the image label just like a button label.
box + f is the form glyph.
a word in an f-box becomes the form title via the label param.
centered f-box gets center_in_region.
0.5 confidence is above the wait floor; uppercase F still maps to form.
box + n is the navbar glyph and always snaps full_width_top, taking precedence over centering.
a word in an n-box routes to the navbar brand label.
the glyph picks the op; navbar snaps to the top band regardless of where the box was drawn.
uppercase N maps to navbar under the case-insensitive rule.
the confidence gate applies before any glyph semantics.
box + v is the video glyph.
uppercase V maps to video under the case-insensitive rule.
two ink colors plus a gradient_direction become a gradient param on the glyph component.
box + ? is the placeholder glyph.
centered ?-box gets center_in_region.
a single letter outside the six-glyph book falls back to placeholder.
unknown glyph falls back to placeholder and still routes the box's word to label.
case-insensitive normalization applies before the book lookup; Q is still unknown -> placeholder.
a word is never a glyph: multi-character glyph normalizes to null, so the box stays a crisp rect.
an empty glyph string normalizes to null: no glyph, no semantics, plain rect.
glyph normalization trims whitespace before the single-character check.
the glyph trigger is a letter in a BOX; on an ellipse it is ignored and the geometric op stands.
glyph ignored on non-rect kinds; the roundish ellipse still snaps square into a circle.
glyph on a line is ignored; the near-horizontal line straightens as usual.
glyph on freeform ink is ignored; smooth_path keeps the user's own shape, never snapped.
glyph ignored on non-rect kinds; a small scribble matching no decorative signature abstains.
glyph on handwriting is ignored; the readable content becomes a text op.
handwriting with no readable content waits regardless of any stray glyph read.
the wait gate is strictly below 0.35, so exactly 0.35 proceeds to the glyph op.
0.34 is below the 0.35 floor: wait wins over a clean glyph read.
the confidence gate fires before the placeholder fallback for out-of-book letters.
gradient styling and the mandatory full_width_top snap compose on a navbar.
label routing happens only when vision attaches the word to the glyph detection; separate handwriting stays its own text op.
handwriting becomes a text op carrying its content in params.text.
phrases are content: preserved verbatim in params.text.

output: {"schema_version":"shapes-1.0","components":[{"op":"text","from":"det_1","params":{"text":"I love baio and I ship faster"}}]}

metadata.rationale: the letter i inside a sentence is word context, never a glyph.
the glyph trigger is a letter in a box; bare handwritten 'i' is content and typesets as text.
'images' starts with the i glyph letter but a word is never a glyph.
'buy now' starts with the b glyph letter but is a phrase, so plain text content.
no glyph, no semantics: 'Login' in a plain box makes a rect with a label, never a button.
a glyph-letter-initial word in a glyphless box stays a rect with a label.
text_writing with empty content is unreadable handwriting: wait.
whitespace-only content trims to nothing and is treated as unreadable.
the confidence gate fires before text handling.
colored handwriting carries fill alongside its content.
two ink colors plus a direction become a gradient param on the text op.
exactly 0.35 confidence proceeds (the wait gate is strictly below the floor).
Plain glyphless rect, mid-page, clearly not square, no ink color: crisp rect op with no params and no snap (omission = none).
Large plain rect (800x400, aspect 0.5): still just a crisp rect; width 800 < 1094.4 band minimum so no band snap.
Small plain rect (120x70, |w-h|/max = 0.42 > 0.15): no square snap, no params.
Elongated ellipse (360x180, ratio diff 0.5 > 0.15 tolerance): ellipse op, no square snap, no params.
Diagonal line: bbox 300x260, minor/major = 0.867 >> 0.15 straighten ratio — kept exactly as drawn, no snap.
Diagonal arrow (320x280, ratio 0.875): arrow op; direction derives from ink endpoints, never from output; no straighten snap.
Open freeform doodle: smooth_path keeps the user's own shape (Catmull-Rom smoothed), never moved or resized — no snap, no params.
Closed freeform doodle in green ink: smooth_path with fill, geometry untouched — the user's silhouette is preserved, snap always omitted.
Freeform doodle with a perfectly square bbox (320x320): smooth_path is NEVER snapped — square applies to rect/ellipse only; the user's shape is sacred.
Handwriting read as content: text op with params.text carrying the exact string; renderer typesets it.
text_writing with null text (vision saw handwriting but could not read it): abstain — wait with reason unreadable_text.
Mid-page scribble with no decorative signature (too narrow for wave, y=550 too low for night_sky, 0 colors for aurora, 300px too big for sparkles): wait ambiguous even at confidence 0.82.
Small colored scribble (140x120, sparkles-sized) but NO handwriting within the 160px radius: sparkles prior requires nearby text, so wait ambiguous.
Three base shapes in one scene: exactly one command per detection, in order, each tied by from; rect plain, line diagonal (no snap), text with content.
Rightward arrow, near-horizontal bbox (420x30, ratio 0.071 <= 0.15): arrow + straighten_h; the head end (rightward) comes from ink endpoints, not the output.
Leftward arrow (head at left end), near-horizontal (380x26, ratio 0.068): same output as rightward — arrow + straighten_h; direction is pure ink geometry.
Upward arrow, near-vertical bbox (28x360, ratio 0.078): arrow + straighten_v.
Downward arrow, near-vertical (32x400, ratio 0.08): arrow + straighten_v; head at bottom end derives from ink.
Near-horizontal line (500x40, minor/major 0.08 <= 0.15): straighten_h to the endpoints' mean y.
Near-vertical line (30x400, ratio 0.075): straighten_v to the endpoints' mean x.
Wobbly horizontal line just INSIDE tolerance (500x70, ratio 0.14 <= 0.15): still straighten_h.
Slightly tilted line just OUTSIDE tolerance (500x90, ratio 0.18 > 0.15): deliberate slope respected — no snap.
Roughly square rect (400x370, |w-h|/max = 0.075 <= 0.15): snap square equalizes about the centroid.
Rect at 400x345 (ratio 0.1375, just inside the 0.15 tolerance): still snaps square.
Rect at 400x300 (ratio 0.25 > 0.15): clearly intentional aspect — no square snap.
Rect at 400x330 (ratio 0.175, just past 0.15): no snap — the tolerance boundary is exclusive above it.
Roundish ellipse (380x350, ratio 0.079): snap square turns it into a clean circle.
Deliberate oval (340x190, ratio 0.44): stays an oval — no square snap.
Plain wide rect hugging the top (w=1250 >= 1094.4 band minimum, y=10 <= 60): full_width_top band per the band rule.
Wide rect at exactly y=60 (the topBandMaxY boundary, inclusive) with w=1150: still full_width_top.
Wide rect touching the bottom (w=1300, y+h=895 >= 900-80=820): full_width_bottom footer band.
Bottom band at the slack boundary: w=1100 >= 1094.4 and y+h=822 >= 820 — just qualifies for full_width_bottom.
Band-wide rect (1200px) but mid-page (y=400, y+h=500): satisfies neither edge condition — no band snap, plain rect.
Rect at y=8 but only 1000px wide (< 0.76 * 1440 = 1094.4): band rule needs BOTH width and edge — no snap.
Plain rect exactly centered (cx = 720): center_in_region applies only to glyph components — a plain rect gets no snap.
Band-wide ellipse hugging the top (1200x90, y=20): the band rule is rect-only — ellipse keeps its ink geometry, no snap.
Single ink color, no gradient direction: params.fill with the color exactly as vision reported it.
Oval in red ink: ellipse with params.fill; not near-square (ratio 0.375) so no snap.
Diagonal line in purple ink: color signal still becomes params.fill (matching dataset convention for lines); no straighten (ratio 0.885).
Near-horizontal red arrow (450x36, ratio 0.08): fill param AND straighten_h snap combine.
Two colors shading downward: params.gradient {colors, direction: down} — colors in vision's reported order.
Two colors shading rightward: gradient with direction right.
Oval shading diagonally between purple and pink: gradient with direction diagonal; not near-square (ratio 0.35) so no snap.
Three colors + downward shading: gradient carries all three colors in vision order.
Two colors but gradient_direction null (no visible shading): NOT a gradient — fill with the first/dominant reported color.
Three colors, no direction: still a plain fill with the first color — gradient requires an observed direction.
gradient_direction set but only ONE color: a gradient needs >= 2 colors, so this degrades to a plain fill.
Default/black-only ink: vision's low-signal rule reports colors as an empty array, so the gold carries NO fill param — the renderer's default styling applies.
Vision may report CSS color NAMES, not just hex: fill copies the string verbatim ('red'); the grader loose-matches case-insensitively.
Multi-word CSS name ('cornflowerblue') passes through verbatim as fill.
Gradient built from CSS names ('red' -> 'gold', down): gradient.colors keep vision's exact strings and order.
3-digit hex shorthand ('#f00') is a valid vision color format: copied verbatim into fill.
Colored handwriting: text op carries BOTH fill (ink color) and text (content) params.
Closed doodle shading purple to pink diagonally: smooth_path + gradient covers the removed blob op — the user's own silhouette, never a generic potato, never snapped.
Near-square rect (380x360, ratio 0.053) with a rightward 2-color gradient: styling and snap combine independently — gradient params + snap square.
Mixed-style scene: gradient rect (hex), CSS-name ellipse fill, and a colorless diagonal line — three detections, three commands, styling handled per detection.
Canonical wave_divider: very wide (1200 >= 864 = 0.6*artboard) short (90 <= 180) scribble at a mid-page section band -> wave_divider with full_width snap; knobs+seed are free values.

Both wave thresholds sit exactly ON the documented boundary and must still trigger: det_1 width == 864 (waveMinWidthFrac*1440, >= is inclusive), det_2 height == 180 (waveMaxHeightPx, <= is inclusive).
Decorative commands do NOT take styleParams: a colored wave scribble still emits only wave knobs (no fill param) — the renderer owns decorative styling.
Canonical night_sky: dark (#0b1026, luminance < 60) wide (1100 >= 700) tall (260 >= 160) scribble hugging the top (y=10 <= 60). Height 260 > 180 keeps it out of the wave branch. No snap.
night_sky with a second bright 'star ink' color: 2 colors also satisfy the aurora gate, but night_sky is checked first in the policy — dark + top wins.
night_sky top-hug boundary: y == 60 (nightSkyMaxY) is inclusive and must still trigger; width 800 < 864 keeps the wave branch out despite h<=... (h=220 > 180 anyway).
night_sky size boundary: width == 700 (nightSkyMinWidth) and height == 160 (nightSkyMinHeight) exactly — both inclusive, still night_sky. Width 700 < 864 so the (h<=180) wave branch cannot claim it.
Canonical aurora_gradient: multicolor (3 >= 2) large (700x250 >= 400x140) scribble in the hero region (y=150 <= 480). palette copies the detection colors; other knobs free.
Every aurora gate exactly at its inclusive threshold: colors == 2 (auroraMinColors), width == 400, height == 140, y == 480 (auroraMaxY) — still aurora_gradient.
Canonical sparkles: small scribble (120x100 <= 200) within 160px of a text_writing detection -> sparkles; the handwriting itself becomes a text op (fill + text params).
Sparkles proximity is symmetric (scribble left of the text, 60px gap < 160) AND the scribble precedes the text in detection order — commands must keep detection order: sparkles first, text second.
Sparkles size gate is inclusive: a 200x200 scribble (== sparklesMaxSizePx on both axes) adjacent to handwriting still becomes sparkles.

All-signature decorated page in one scene: night_sky (dark top band), heading text, sparkles beside it, mid-page wave, and a centered glyph button (label routed, center_in_region: |cx-720| = 0 <= 48). Order preserved.
confidence 0.2 < waitConfidence 0.35 -> wait('low_confidence'); kind is irrelevant once the confidence gate fails.
EVERY detection below 0.35 -> all-wait output. Note det_2 (readable text) and det_3 (perfect wave signature) still wait: the confidence gate precedes kind/glyph/decorative logic.
Confident text_writing with null text OR whitespace-only text -> wait('unreadable_text') (policy trims before checking emptiness).
Stray tiny scribble (45x35) with no handwriting anywhere: small enough for sparkles but nearText fails -> wait('ambiguous').
A textbook wave signature (1200x90) at confidence 0.3 must abstain with low_confidence, not become wave_divider — abstention outranks the decorative prior.
Mixed abstention: confident circle-ish ellipse (360x360 -> snap square) and text proceed; the 0.28-confidence smooth_path waits. One command per detection, in order.

Wave near-misses on each conjunct: det_1 width 850 < 864 (just under waveMinWidthFrac), det_2 height 181 > 180 (just over waveMaxHeightPx). Neither matches any other signature -> wait('ambiguous'), not wave_divider.
Dark wide scribble NOT hugging the top (y=200 > 60): night_sky prior requires the top band -> wait('ambiguous') (h=250 > 180 blocks wave; 1 color blocks aurora).
Top-hugging wide scribble in BRIGHT ink (#f59e0b, luminance >= 60): night_sky requires at least one dark color -> wait('ambiguous').
Empty colors array: geometrically perfect night_sky position/size but colors=[] fails the dark-ink check (and every other signature) -> wait('ambiguous').
Aurora near-misses: det_1 has 2 colors but y=481 > auroraMaxY 480 (one px below the hero region); det_2 is large and hero-positioned but single-color (< auroraMinColors 2). Both -> wait('ambiguous').
Small scribble adjacent to a RECT (not text_writing): the sparkles prior needs handwriting nearby -> wait('ambiguous'); the rect crisps normally.
Small scribble 165px right of the text bbox edge: 405 < 100+140+160=400 fails (radius 160 is exclusive at this gap) -> wait('ambiguous'); the text itself proceeds.
Scribble beside handwriting but width 210 > sparklesMaxSizePx 200 -> not sparkles, no other signature -> wait('ambiguous').

Dark full-width RECT at the top looks like night_sky, but decorative signatures apply to kind=scribble only: a rect stays a rect — here a top band (w=1200 >= 1094.4, y=10 <= 60) -> rect + full_width_top with dark fill.

Precedence trap: dark top-hugging scribble that satisfies BOTH signatures (y=20<=60, w=1200>=700, h=170>=160, dark) — but 1200>=864 and 170<=180 hit the wave branch first, so gold is wave_divider, not night_sky.
Precedence trap: multicolor hero-region scribble that also matches aurora (2 colors, 900x150, y=300) — the wave branch (w>=864, h<=180) is checked first, so gold is wave_divider.
waitConfidence is a strict less-than: confidence == 0.35 exactly PROCEEDS (det_1 -> rect), 0.34 waits (det_2). Tests both sides of the documented boundary.
Glyphs opt into semantics only on kind=rect: a smooth_path carrying glyph 'b' and text 'Login' stays smooth_path with NO params (no label routing, no fill) — the user's own shape, never snapped.
Glyph 'i' on an ellipse is ignored (glyph book is box-only): near-round ellipse (360x360) -> ellipse + snap square, fill from ink.
Glyph 'v' on a scribble is ignored; the scribble is small and beside handwriting so the decorative prior wins -> sparkles (not video).
Single letters outside the glyph book fall back to placeholder: 'z' box (centered, cx=720 -> center_in_region) and '7' box (off-center, no snap).
A multi-character 'glyph' ('ok') is not a glyph (a word is never a glyph; normGlyph -> null): the box stays a plain crisp rect with no params.
Glyphs are case-insensitive: 'B' -> button; nearby word routes to params.label ('Buy now'), ink color to fill; cx=610 is 110px off-center so no center snap.
Glyph is trimmed before matching: ' n ' -> navbar; text 'baio' routes to label (brand); navbar always snaps full_width_top.
An n-glyph box drawn mid-page (y=400) is STILL a navbar with snap full_width_top: the glyph decides the op and the navbar policy is unconditional on position.
'?' is in the glyph book -> placeholder; off-center (cx=1050), no colors -> bare command with no params and no snap.
Empty colors arrays produce commands with NO params key at all: bare rect, and a near-horizontal arrow (20/500 = 0.04 <= 0.15) with only snap straighten_h.
Gradient needs BOTH 2+ colors AND a direction: det_1 (2 colors + down) -> params.gradient; det_2 (2 colors, null direction) -> plain fill with the FIRST color only.

Plain-rect band snaps at the edges: det_1 bottom band (y+h=895 >= 820, w=1200 >= 1094.4) -> full_width_bottom; det_2 top band (y=58 <= 60, w=1100 >= 1094.4) -> full_width_top; det_3 y=61 misses the top band by 1px -> no snap.
Top-touching rect at width 1080 < bandMinWidthFrac*1440 = 1094.4: not wide enough for a band -> plain rect, no snap.
straightenRatio 0.15 is inclusive: det_1 60/400 = 0.15 exactly -> straighten_h; det_2 61/400 > 0.15 -> no snap; det_3 tall thin arrow 14/280 -> straighten_v.
squareTolerance 0.15 is inclusive: 400x340 -> |60|/400 = 0.15 exactly -> snap square; 400x339 -> 0.1525 -> no snap.

Two detections with nearly identical bboxes but different kinds diverge completely: the rect crisps (square snap), the overlapping scribble becomes sparkles (small + near the text). from ids must not be swapped.
Detections arrive with non-sequential ids (det_4, det_1, det_3, det_2): commands must follow ARRAY order, not id order — text, image, arrow, wave.
Prefix-colliding ids (det_1, det_10, det_11) must be echoed exactly: det_1 proceeds, det_10 waits on confidence, det_11 (near-round ellipse) snaps square.

The sparkles proximity check reads sibling KIND only, not confidence: the text detection abstains (0.3 -> wait) yet still anchors the adjacent small scribble as sparkles. Flagged in decorative-ambiguous.md.

Six-detection landing page mixing glyphs + decorative + bands: navbar (glyph), aurora (3-color hero scribble), heading, sparkles, centered labeled button, footer band. Command order must match detection order exactly.

Eight detections spanning every branch: night_sky, styled text, sparkles, off-center labeled button, straighten_h line, wave, low-confidence wait, and a stray tiny scribble too far from any text (ambiguous wait). Strict 1:1 in order.
A word in a plain box is content, not a glyph: 'Login' in a glyph-less rect -> rect with params.label 'Login' (NOT a button).
smooth_path with 2 colors + diagonal direction gets params.gradient (this is the removed 'blob' covered) but NEVER a snap — the user's silhouette is kept exactly.
